sections.heading: C - Section Thirteen: Seniors and Driving
sections.markdown:
## C - Section Thirteen: Seniors and Driving

FACT_ID: sec13-F01 | anchor: A01
Senior driving demands physical, visual, and mental ability, and the day may come to limit or stop driving temporarily or permanently [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec13-F02 | anchor: A01
Unsafe-driver warning signs run getting lost in familiar places, dents and scrapes on cars and property, and frequent close calls or collisions [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec13-F03 | anchor: A01
Senior drivers may curb night driving with lit routes when necessary, favor light-traffic hours, dodge hard intersections, shorten trips to essentials, skip freeways, and add a right-side mirror [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec13-F04 | anchor: A01
The Driver Skills Self-Assessment Questionnaire lives at dmv.ca.gov/driver-skills [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec13-F05 | anchor: A01
Drivers 70 or older at expiry renew in person with a vision test and possibly other exams, eligible for eLearning knowledge tests when required, with renewal notices mailed about 90 days out and missing notices answered by applications at dmv.ca.gov/dlservices or offices plus samples at dmv.ca.gov/driver-ed [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec13-F06 | anchor: A01
The Community Liaison champions public safety for all Californians with senior and teen focus, mediating fair, lawful, dignified treatment, barred from hearing and reexamination representation yet rich in tools and information [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec13-F07 | anchor: A02
Area outreach and liaison contact runs through Community Liaison and Outreach at eight three three, four nine three, zero six seven five [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0089]

FACT_ID: sec13-F08 | anchor: A02
Progressive dementia ultimately ends safe driving, leaving caregivers, physicians, and law enforcement to halt seniors and arrange other transport, with reexamination details at dmv.ca.gov/reexamination [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0089]

FACT_ID: sec13-F09 | anchor: A02
The Mature Driver Improvement Program runs eight hours for drivers 55 and older on topics of special mature-driver interest [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0089]

FACT_ID: sec13-F10 | anchor: A02
Insurers may discount program graduates on proof of completion certificates valid three years and renewable through four-hour refresher courses from DMV-approved providers listed at dmv.ca.gov/seniors [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0089]

FACT_ID: sec13-F11 | anchor: A02
Drivers 62 and older qualify for no-fee Senior ID cards, unsafe drivers of any age may trade licenses for no-fee ID cards good for identification only, and details live at dmv.ca.gov/id-cards [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0089]
